description: Evals for the check-bash-read PreToolUse hook

evals.name: cat-large-file
evals.reason: Plain cat on large file — should block

evals.name: cat-small-file
evals.reason: Small file — not worth delegating

evals.name: cat-with-flag
evals.reason: cat with -n flag — should still block

evals.name: head-large-file
evals.reason: head on large file — should block

evals.name: head-with-count
evals.reason: head -100 — still a bulk read, block

evals.name: tail-large-file
evals.reason: tail on large file — should block

evals.name: less-large-file
evals.reason: less on large file — should block

evals.name: cat-pipe
evals.reason: Piped command — targeted read

evals.name: cat-redirect
evals.reason: Redirect — copying file, not reading into context

evals.name: non-read-command
evals.reason: Not a file read command

evals.name: grep-command
evals.reason: grep is a targeted search — not caught

evals.name: cat-quoted-path
evals.reason: Quoted path — should still be caught

evals.name: cat-nonexistent
evals.reason: File doesn't exist — let Bash handle the error

evals.name: empty-command
evals.reason: Empty command — pass through

evals.name: missing-command-field
evals.reason: No command field — pass through

evals.name: more-large-file
evals.reason: more on large file — only regex-matched command without coverage

evals.name: head-n-space-count
evals.reason: Parser bug: -n and 5 are separate args, 5 is treated as file path — file '5' won't exist so allow

evals.name: cat-quoted-path-with-space
evals.reason: Quoted path containing a space — word-split-on-space parsing must not break this into two bogus tokens and fall through to allow

evals.name: cat-complex-code-over-threshold
evals.reason: Fidelity axis: real 405-line file with race-sensitive lock/retry/circuit-breaker logic in its sampled head. A cheap worker's summary would flatten exactly the details (lock ordering, half-open probe exclusivity) that make this code correct, so the gate should keep it in context even past the line threshold.

evals.name: cat-simple-log-over-threshold
evals.reason: Fidelity axis: real 400-line access log, one repetitive record shape per line. A worker's summary loses nothing a human or Claude would act on, so once the cost axis clears the threshold this should delegate.

evals.name: head-complex-code-small-slice
evals.reason: Cost axis: head -30 only ingests 30 lines regardless of the file's 405-line total, so this stays under threshold and allows on cost alone — independent of the file's complexity.

evals.name: cat-simple-data-under-threshold
evals.reason: Cost axis: real 60-line simple CSV export, well under the 350-line threshold — allowed regardless of the fidelity axis because the volume never clears the gate.

evals.name: sh-c-wrapped-more-large
evals.reason: Bypass seen in Codex after a block: the same read wrapped in /bin/sh -c must be judged as the inner read.

evals.name: absolute-path-more-large
evals.reason: Bypass seen in Codex after a block: an absolute path to the read command must match like the bare name.

evals.name: zsh-lc-wrapped-cat-large
evals.reason: Combined flags (-lc) still carry -c, so the wrapped read is unwrapped and gated.

evals.name: sh-c-wrapped-cat-small
evals.reason: Unwrapping must not change the verdict for a small file.

evals.name: sh-c-wrapped-cat-piped-outside
evals.reason: A pipe outside the wrapper is a targeted read, same as the unwrapped cat-pipe case.

evals.name: sh-runs-script-file
evals.reason: Without -c the shell runs the file as a script instead of printing it, so there is nothing to gate.

evals.name: bash-O-option-wrapped-cat-large
evals.reason: -O takes a separate shopt name; skipping it must still reach -c and gate the wrapped read.

evals.name: bash-rcfile-wrapped-cat-large
evals.reason: --rcfile takes a separate file argument; it must not be mistaken for the command or stop the unwrap before -c.

evals.name: bash-sh-two-level-nested-cat-large
evals.reason: Two nested wrappers with alternating quote styles unwrap to the inner read.

evals.name: bash-sh-escaped-quote-cat-large
evals.reason: Escaped quotes cannot be safely tokenized by xargs; the wrapper must fail closed instead of allowing the read.

evals.name: cat-large-stderr-to-devnull
evals.reason: Only stderr is redirected; the file's content still reaches context, so the read is gated like a plain cat.

evals.name: cat-large-stderr-to-stdout
evals.reason: 2>&1 merges stderr into stdout, which still reaches context.

evals.name: cat-large-stdout-to-stderr
evals.reason: Stdout sent to stderr still lands in the assistant's context; only a file target keeps it out.

evals.name: cat-large-append-to-file
evals.reason: Stdout appended to a file — copying, not reading into context.

evals.name: cat-large-both-to-file
evals.reason: Stdout and stderr both sent to a file — nothing reaches context.

evals.name: sh-c-wrapped-cat-large-stderr-to-devnull
evals.reason: A stderr-only redirect inside the wrapper does not keep the unwrapped read out of context.

evals.name: cat-simple-log-exact-purpose

tool_input.description: Find the exact request order and timestamps before the first 500 error to debug its root cause

evals.reason: Purpose axis: same 400-line log as case 20, but the stated purpose needs exact order and timestamps, which a worker's summary drops — keep it in context.

evals.name: cat-simple-log-overview-purpose

tool_input.description: Get an overview of what kinds of requests this access log contains

evals.reason: Purpose axis: an overview-level purpose survives a worker's summary, so the simple 400-line log is delegated as in case 20.
